'''Angelica M. Stacy''' is the associate vice provost for the faculty, and professor of chemistry, at [[University of California, Berkeley]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ofew.berkeley.edu/associate-vice-provost-angelica-stacy|title=Associate Vice Provost Angelica Stacy {{!}} Office for Faculty Equity & Welfare|website=ofew.berkeley.edu|access-date=2019-04-03}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://chemistry.berkeley.edu/faculty/chem/stacy|title=Angelica Stacy {{!}} College of Chemistry|website=chemistry.berkeley.edu|access-date=2019-04-03}}</ref> Stacy was one of the first women to receive tenure in the college of chemistry at [[UC Berkeley]].

At UC Berkeley, Stacy leads a research group that explores topics in materials science and chemistry education.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Stacy |first1=Angelica |title=The Stacy Group |url=http://www.cchem.berkeley.edu/amsgrp/index.html |website=cchem.berkeley.edu |access-date=26 June 2021}}</ref> Stacy has won numerous awards for her contributions to chemistry education research and has advocated for increased diversity in the field and STEM more generally.<ref>{{Cite web |title=02.05.2003 - Faculty diversity: the road ahead |url=https://newsarchive.berkeley.edu/news/berkeleyan/2003/02/05_facdv.html |access-date=2026-04-24 |website=newsarchive.berkeley.edu}}</ref>

== Research, career, and service ==
Stacy received a B.A. in physics and chemistry magna cum laude at [[LaSalle College]] (1977).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://digitalcommons.lasalle.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?referer=https://www.google.com/&httpsredir=1&article=1045&context=commencement_programs|title=La Salle College Commencement 1977|last=|first=|date=|website=|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref> Stacy would then go on to receive her Ph.D. from [[Cornell University]] (1981) with Professor [[Michell J Sienko]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://academictree.org/chemistry/peopleinfo.php?pid=59390|title=Chemistry Tree - Angelica M. Stacy|website=academictree.org|access-date=2019-04-08}}</ref> She was a postdoctoral fellow at [[Northwestern University]] (1981–1983) with Professor [[Richard van Duyne]]<ref>{{Cite journal|date=2016-09-22|title=List of Students of Richard P. Van Duyne|journal=The Journal of Physical Chemistry C|volume=120|issue=37|pages=20486–20489|doi=10.1021/acs.jpcc.6b01840|issn=1932-7447}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sites.northwestern.edu/vanduyne/members/alumni/|title=Van Duyne Research Group » Alumni|website=sites.northwestern.edu|access-date=2019-05-06}}</ref> and Professor Peter Stair<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://chemgroups.northwestern.edu/stair/|title=Peter C. Stair Research Group :: Northwestern University|website=chemgroups.northwestern.edu|access-date=2019-05-08}}</ref> prior to beginning her faculty position in the college of chemistry at the [[University of California, Berkeley]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://academictree.org/chemistry/peopleinfo.php?pid=59390|title=Chemistry Tree - Angelica M. Stacy|website=academictree.org|access-date=2019-04-08}}</ref> As a junior faculty member at Berkeley, Stacy was the first recipient of the Prytanean Faculty Award, which is an unrestricted grant awarded to distinguished female faculty members at UC Berkeley.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.dailycal.org/2018/01/18/female-alumni-association-honors-uc-berkeley-law-professor-25k-grant/|title = All-female alumni association honors UC Berkeley law professor with 25K grant|date = 19 January 2018}}</ref>

In the area of service, and as a senior member of the faculty at the [[University of California]], Stacy has been outspoken about her commitment to issues surrounding diversity and equity in the sciences. Stacy has served as co-investigator and [[principal investigator]] of the University of California Faculty Family-Friendly Edge,<ref>[https://ucfamilyedge.berkeley.edu/ University of California Faculty Family-Friendly Edge]</ref> which is a [[Alfred P. Sloan Foundation|Sloan Foundation]] research project based at UC Berkeley. In these roles and that of associate vice provost of the faculty at the University of California, Berkeley, Stacy is particularly committed to promoting "data-driven initiatives to increase equity and inclusion in faculty recruitment, advancement, and retention".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ucop.edu/ucadvance/_files/roundtable-3/speaker-biographies.pdf|title=Mentoring Faculty in an Inclusive Climate: Supporting Women and URM STEM Faculty at UC|last=|first=|date=|website=|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref>

In addition to her research in the area of chemistry education at the university level, Stacy has been outspoken on the importance of exposure to chemistry research (and research in the sciences more generally) at the high school level to help promote interest in career pathways in basic research, as a pathway to improve diversity in the field, and as a strategy to enhance student learning outcomes. She has spoken on the importance of high school educators as key to these endeavors:

'''"'''I have to come to the defense of my high school colleagues. Nothing is going to change until we respect them as professionals. They have a lot to offer. They have many ideas, but no time. They are in contact with students every hour of the day. There are no longer in-service days or professional days in many states. High school teachers know what they would like to do, but they have no time to do it. Yet we treat them as if we need to go and help them. In fact, I think we have much to learn from them. Until we come to the table with our high school colleagues, acknowledging them as the high-level professionals that they are, things are not going to change."<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK44903/|title=Keeping an Eye to the Future in Designing Graduate Programs|last=Roundtable|first=National Research Council (US) Chemical Sciences|date=2000|publisher=National Academies Press (US)|language=en}}</ref>

Stacy is also the author of the book ''Living by Chemistry'', a research-based curriculum for students at the high school level.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://eric.ed.gov/?id=ED481213|title=Perspective of a Chemist: A Framework to Promote Conceptual Understanding of Chemistry|last1=Claesgens|first1=Jennifer|last2=Scalise|first2=Kathleen|last3=Draney|first3=Karen|last4=Wilson|first4=Mark|last5=Stacy|first5=Angelica|date=April 2002|language=en}}</ref>

== Awards ==
Stacy has been recognized for her contributions to chemistry education through numerous awards at the national and local level:<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://chemistry.berkeley.edu/faculty/chem/stacy|title=Angelica Stacy {{!}} College of Chemistry|website=chemistry.berkeley.edu|access-date=2019-04-03}}</ref>

*[[Garvan-Olin Medal]], [[American Chemical Society]] 1995<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.acs.org/content/acs/en/funding-and-awards/awards/national/bytopic/francis-p-garvan-john-m-olin-medal.html|title=Francis P. Garvan-John M. Olin Medal|website=American Chemical Society|language=en|access-date=2019-05-06}}</ref>
*Distinguished Teaching Scholar, [[National Science Foundation]] (2005)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.berkeley.edu/news/media/releases/2005/06/21_stacy.shtml|title=06.21.2005 - UC Berkeley chemist Angelica Stacy receives national teaching award|website=www.berkeley.edu|access-date=2019-04-04}}</ref>
*[[James Flack Norris]] Award for Outstanding Achievement in Teaching Chemistry, [[American Chemical Society]] (1998)<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nesacs.org/awards/norris/awards_norris_recipients.html|title=Welcome to NESACS - Awards {{!}} James Flack Norris Award Recipients|website=www.nesacs.org|access-date=2019-05-02}}</ref>
*President's Chair for Teaching, [[University of California]] (1993-1996)
*Award for Professional Excellence, [[Iota Sigma Pi Society]] (1996)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.iotasigmapi.info/|title=Iota Sigma Pi - A National Honor Society for Women in Chemistry|website=www.iotasigmapi.info|access-date=2019-05-02}}</ref>
*Noyce Prize for Excellence in Undergraduate Teaching (Chemistry), [[University of California, Berkeley]] (1996)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://chemistry.berkeley.edu/awards-honors#noyce|title=Major Awards & Honors {{!}} College of Chemistry|website=chemistry.berkeley.edu|access-date=2019-05-02}}</ref>
*Catalyst Award, Chemical Manufacturers Association (1995)
*Francis P. Garvan-John M. Olin Medal, [[American Chemical Society]] (1994)
*Technology Transfer Certificate of Merit, [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]] (1991)
*Faculty Award for Women Scientists and Engineers, [[National Science Foundation]] (1991)
*Berkeley Distinguished Teaching Award, [[University of California, Berkeley]] (1991)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://chemistry.berkeley.edu/awards-honors|title=Major Awards & Honors {{!}} College of Chemistry|website=chemistry.berkeley.edu|access-date=2019-05-02}}</ref>
*[[Sloan Foundation]] Fellowship (1988-1990)
*Teacher-Scholar Award, [[Camille and Henry Dreyfus Foundation]] (1988)
*[[ExxonMobil]] Award Faculty Fellowship for Solid State Chemistry, [[American Chemical Society]] (1987)<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://acsdic.org/wordpress/awards/exxonmobil-award/|title=ExxonMobil Award|website=Division of Inorganic Chemistry|language=en-US|access-date=2019-05-02}}</ref>
*Prytanean Society Faculty Enrichment Award, [[University of California, Berkeley]] (1986)
*Presidential Young Investigator, [[National Science Foundation]] (1984-1989)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=8351881|title=NSF Award Search: Award#8351881 - Presidential Young Investigator Award/Synthesis and Characterization of New Materials|website=www.nsf.gov|access-date=2019-05-02}}</ref>
